newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil stagnates in very quiet market.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil stagnates in very quiet market.

text.p: NWE gas oil was steady on Friday in a lacklustre market with the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States and continued uncertainty over the record 865,800 tonne delivery into the IPE November contract dampening trade.

Heating oil barge premiums were unchanged at Dec IPE +$1.50/ +$2.50 a tonne for second half delivery. Traders said the market was very quiet. A major refiner shifted a parcel for second half delivery at $219.50 a tonne, which was $1.50 over the screen when the deal was done.

The final delivery day for the November IPE gas oil contract falls on Saturday and many traders said they were standing back until Monday in the hope they would have a better idea of the outcome of the stand-off between Cargill and AIC.
"We just don't know whether we're going to be long or short," said one trader. "The picture should get a bit clearer as of Monday."
The arb into Asia remains open, but no more deals beyond the 60,000 tonne Russian cargo done into Singapore at means quotes +37.5 cents a barrel, reported on Thursday, were heard.
Shipping sources said Cargill had fixed the 49,000 tonne Samos to carry gas oil from Europe to India loading December 5.
